P1.evidence: No setter on this call — the title carries no setter code and no setter was referenced — so the read-back check does not apply. Roughly three minutes of rapport preceded the frame, which was again two-part plus alignment: 'calls basic really, I just want to get a good idea where you're at, really build out what it is you want, and then... let's talk about it, see if there's some alignment there, if not it's fine as well.' No agreement question; the prospect talked over the frame to start. Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Training history and diet were covered thoroughly — 'Are you training at all right now?', 'What were you doing when you were training in the past?' and 'What is it that you eat?' produced a detailed picture. But the load-bearing facts arrived because the prospect volunteered fifteen minutes of unprompted medical history, not because anyone screened for it. Not one direct health-conditions question was asked of a man with active autoimmune disease, SIBO, painful bladder syndrome and a repaired AC separation — the AC separation surfaced by accident at 00:36:37 and the rep did not follow up on it at all. No age, no height, no weight. Sleep was never asked despite the prospect describing needing to sleep for two weeks to recover from training.

P3.evidence: The prioritisation question ran cleanly — 'for you, is the big thing, the realignment more so than anything else? Or is there any other things?' — and produced a clear hierarchy of alignment first, then mass. The reflect-back was the best in the batch: 'So it's essentially rebuilding the foundation initially, get everything back into alignment, have the body and the nervous system use everything as a system as it should be used, and then once that foundation's rebuilt, you then want to build upon that and build the mass.' Confirmed. But the deep half never ran despite the richest possible material sitting in the open — childhood trauma, a career built on emotional embodiment, an explicit belief that lifting can process trauma. The rep engaged with all of it as conversation and none of it as discovery. Nobody else's stake was raised at any point in fifty-nine minutes.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were mapped well — Functional Patterns, martial arts, max-effort hypertrophy work — and what happened with each was drawn out in detail, including the trainer's fix of lifting for time rather than to failure. The prospect effectively named his own gap, that hard training triggers crashes and he lacks a way to titrate load. What never ran is the structural reframe: no 'why do you feel it didn't stick', no 'what's the one thing actually getting in the way', and no 'the information isn't the problem'. Given that his blocker is physiological rather than motivational, the scripted framing would have needed adapting, but the rep did not attempt it in any form.

P5.evidence: Never ran. No two-year projection, no settling question, no line in the sand. The prospect supplied his own version unprompted — a harrowing account of blood in his throat and urine, C. diff, thrush, and walking through anxiety every morning — and it was received as conversation rather than converted into any consequence frame.

P6.evidence: The belief question was never asked. The all-in question effectively ran, but only after the deferral and in improvised form: 'I guess I'm just out of curiosity, what's the 1%?' — a good move that correctly surfaced the real blocker as the practitioner conversation rather than money. Before the price the rep took process alignment as commitment: 'In terms of like a process, how do you feel about it?' answered 'I like that it's simple... I feel good about that.' That is approval of a description, not a commitment to act.

P11.evidence: No attempt to collect payment — the mechanism was described ('We just do it on a credit card') but nothing was processed and no link was sent. The Trevor onboarding call was described in detail and tentatively slotted for Tuesday or Wednesday with an hour blocked rather than thirty minutes, but never booked. No agreement, nothing signed. Partial on the last step only for repeated instruction to complete the onboarding form thoroughly and to bring the medical PDFs to Trevor; no welcome email and no Skool link.

objection_plays.detail: The decisive objection on this call, and the documented script gap. The prospect gated the purchase on his functional medicine practitioner — 'I was to talk to Mark about what he thinks about my body's ability to be able to handle this' — which is a clinical-fit objection, and the playbook has no play for it. What the rep improvised is the problem: rather than supporting the clearance step, he engineered around it by decoupling onboarding from the start date, so that payment and onboarding could complete before any clinician was consulted — 'if Mark says, do it in a week, do it in a month, you're still prepared and set up for everything to the point where it's a click of a finger you start.' He also volunteered an unqualified physiological claim, that 'the mobility stuff, it doesn't tax a CNS', to a man whose presenting problem is a cytokine-driven crash response. The script needs a play here that routes toward clearance, not around it.

'Can you give me till Monday... I feel 99% I'm going to do it' is an OA trigger. One move ran, and it was the right one: 'what's the 1%?', which is functionally 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started' and correctly isolated the real blocker. Nothing else ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now', no final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in.' Having isolated the blocker the rep did not then work it.

'Would I want to start next week, or do I want to wait a couple weeks and let my body settle in' is an OD trigger in form. None of the scripted moves ran — and correctly so, since 'things never slow down' and 'the only thing you can control is right now' would be actively inappropriate against a medically-grounded timing concern. The rep instead removed the timing question from the decision altogether. Recorded as partial rather than miss because a deliberate and coherent alternative was run, but it is the same manoeuvre described in the clinical gap above.

Money was raised and self-resolved in a single breath — 'I also want to look at the money... the money I don't think will be a big deal at all. I just spent 50-some K on another coaching package for my business.' No play was needed, yet the rep responded by offering to break the payment up: 'you can break it up as well... I'd either suggest doing it upfront or you can do it in two payments.' Volunteering a concession to a prospect who has just told you price is irrelevant, and who then says he would rather pay in full for the credit card points, is the second instance of pre-emptive discounting in this batch.

notes: Excellent rapport and the sharpest reflect-back in the batch, on the most medically complex prospect in it — and the two things that needed to happen did not. P5 and the belief check never ran, so an hour of extraordinarily rich emotional material produced no leverage; and when the prospect named a clinician gate as his single biggest concern, the rep's instinct was to make the sale independent of it. Coach that specific move: when a prospect says a doctor needs to sign this off, the correct play is to make clearance the next step, not to route the onboarding around it.
